context: Whole group gathers for a midsummer evening; many warm voices.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 夏の夜、皆おって、ええなぁ。
lines.en: Summer nights like this — having everyone here, it's just right.
lines.style: Slow, measured Kansai cadence. Warm contentment in the opening. Light pause before 'it's just right,' as if savoring the moment. The voice of someone who has learned to notice what matters.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 夜空、明かり、ようけ綺麗や!
lines.en: Look at the sky — all those lights are so beautiful!
lines.style: Bright, brassy Kansai energy. Quick attack on the opening. Generous enthusiasm — not performing, genuinely delighted. A little breathless on 'beautiful,' like she can't quite contain the joy.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.en: Moments like these warm you right down to your heart.
lines.style: Soft, reverent delivery. Slight breathiness beneath. Slow pace, like she's speaking from somewhere tender and true. Trailing off gently at the end, inviting others into the feeling.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 皆と、こうやって、過ごせて感謝や。
lines.en: I'm grateful we get to spend time like this together.
lines.style: Warm, grounded Kansai tone. Gentle earnestness — not effusive, just genuine. Steady pace. A quiet strength in the simplicity of it. The voice of someone who means what he says.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Eager, bright child's voice with real anticipation. Light and quick. Slight lift on the question, genuine curiosity. The kind of impatience that's still hopeful, not demanding.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: Nights like this — I'm really happy.
lines.style: Soft, sincere, without precocity. Warm simplicity. Slight pause after the dash, collecting the feeling. Small voice, but certain. The kind of happiness that doesn't need explaining.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 長く、皆で、こうしような。
lines.en: Let's stay like this together for a long time.
lines.style: Quiet Kansai warmth. Slow, deliberate. Not a command, more a gentle wish. Weight in each phrase — the voice of someone who knows how rare and precious this is.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: お弁当、ようけ作ったで!
lines.en: I made plenty of food — lots of bento!
lines.style: Animated Kansai pride and generosity. Quick, bright delivery. A little puffed up with the pleasure of providing. Warmth that comes from feeding the people you love.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.en: Family — you really are a treasure.
lines.style: Soft, reverential tone. Slight breathiness. Slow, intentional pacing. Not casual. The kind of sincerity that costs something to speak aloud. Tender trailing-off.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Warm Kansai contentment. Unhurried delivery. Light satisfaction in the opening, gentle pause before 'truly.' The voice of someone settled into something good.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: I love you all so much.
lines.style: Bright, clear child's voice. Unguarded warmth. Quick, simple delivery — no hesitation, no performance. The kind of love that children express without filter.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: ずっと、こうやって、続けたい。
lines.en: I want nights like this to go on forever.
lines.style: Soft, wistful, but grounded. Gentle urgency beneath — not desperate, just hoping hard. Slow pace. Slightly breathy. The voice of someone learning what it means to want to hold onto something.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.en: There's so much to be grateful for — truly, so much.
lines.style: Quiet, humble Kansai elder. Slow, reflective pace. Weight on 'grateful.' Not heavy, but full. The kind of gratitude that comes from a long life of paying attention. Gentle trailing-off, like a prayer.
